 Summarising any important new efficacy/effectiveness information that has become available

f.title: Make the level of detail proportional to the product's known or emerging important benefits and risks
f.statement: The level of detail in PBRER sections that evaluate safety data, efficacy/effectiveness data, safety signals and benefit-risk should depend on the product's known or emerging important benefits and risks. signals, and benefit-risk. Therefore, the extent of information provided in such PBRER sections will
vary among individual PBRERs.

information should be included, plus the relevant benefit information, in order to facilitate a robust
benefit-risk analysis. Conversely, when little new important safety information has become available
during the reporting interval, a concise summary of baseline benefit information should be sufficient,

f.title: Consider context of use and the nature and clinical importance of key benefits and risks in the evaluation
f.statement: The benefit-risk evaluation should consider: the context of use (condition treated, prevented or diagnosed; its severity and seriousness; the population treated); for key benefits, their nature, clinical importance, duration, generalisability, evidence in non-responders to other therapies, effect size and all individual elements of benefit; and for risks, their clinical importance (nature of toxicity, seriousness, frequency, predictability, preventability, reversibility, impact on patients) and whether they arose from off-label use, a new use or misuse.

rows.quote:
Consider the context of use of the medicinal product: the condition to be treated, prevented, or
diagnosed; its severity and seriousness; and the population to be treated.
 With respect to key benefit(s), consider its nature, clinical importance, duration, and
generalizability, as well as evidence of efficacy in non-responders to other therapies and
alternative treatments. Consider the effect size. If there are individual elements of benefit,
consider all (e.g., for therapies for arthritis: reduction of symptoms and inhibition of radiographic
progression of joint damage).
 With respect to risk, consider its clinical importance, e.g., nature of toxicity, seriousness,
frequency, predictability, preventability, reversibility, impact on patients, and whether it arose
from off-label use, a new use, or misuse.

f.title: Classify as identified risk an untoward occurrence with adequate evidence of association with the product
